Darth Plagueis took place basically as a prequel of the first movie, but ends around the same time as the first movie ends (it focuses on Palpatine's Sith master Plagueis) and really gave much more context to all the midi chlorian talk in the first movie. It even made the explanation for Anakin's immaculate conception perfectly plausible.

Rise of Darth Vader takes place just as the third movie is ending and through the next couple of weeks/months. It gives a TON more context to why Anakin betrayed the Jedi and, again, makes it perfectly plausible.

If these two books had been added to the movies, then I think that the prequel trilogy wouldn't be regarded as poorly as it is. (Of course that's the advantage of books, you can go into a lot more back story which would be boring on film, or give light to the thoughts and motivations of a character easier.)

I've got a few more Star Wars expanded universe books in line to read (reading Tarkin currently, also have Millennium Falcon and Heir to the Jedi next), but I'm actually getting more and more interested in the expanded universe since I ran out of books to read in the Star Trek expanded universe.
